from.place: ## Proof: passage from the Cech cohomology of [lem-pc-cech-computes] (all index tuples) to the alternating Cech complex indexed by subsets

title: The alternating Cech complex computes Cech cohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal U:X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering, viewed as a covering of the Zariski site of $X$ [def-sc-zariski-site], with Cech complex $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ and Cech cohomology $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] for a presheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $X$. Choose a total order $<$ on $I$ and write $U_{i_0\dots i_p}=U_{i_0}\cap\dots\cap U_{i_p}$. The *alternating (ordered) Cech complex* $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ has $\check{\mathcal C}^p_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{i_0<\dots<i_p}\mathcal F(U_{i_0\dots i_p})$ for $p\ge0$, zero for $p<0$, and differential $d(s)_{i_0\dots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j\,s_{i_0\dots\hat{i_j}\dots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\dots i_{p+1}}}$. Then restricting a cochain to the strictly increasing index tuples is a cochain map $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$, and it induces isomorphisms $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\cong H^p(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet_{\mathrm{alt}}(\mathcal U,\mathcal F))$ for all $p\ge0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 20.23 (Cech cohomology: the alternating and ordered Cech complexes), the lemma that the ordered Cech complex is homotopy equivalent to the full Cech complex

proof.text: Define increasing-tuple cochains as the product of sections on increasing tuples, and define its differential by the signed face sum. Define degree restriction by evaluation at the underlying increasing tuple; it commutes with the full differential by the formula. Restriction is degreewise surjective by extension by zero to other tuples, so it is an epimorphism of abelian groups. Precomposing the square of the increasing-tuple differential with this epimorphism gives the full differential squared followed by restriction, hence zero. Cancel the epimorphism to obtain d squared = 0, and construct the cochain complex A with CochainComplex.of. The degree identifications e are identities, and CochainComplex.ofHom constructs r. The two displayed coordinate formulas are definitional.

Apply the homotopy inverse lemma to this explicitly constructed A, e and r, using the proved restriction formula. Form HomotopyEquiv with the supplied inverse and both homotopies. Mathlib HomotopyEquiv.toHomologyIso gives in each degree an isomorphism whose hom is homologyMap r. Therefore IsIso (homologyMap r p) holds for every p. The cover hypothesis is preserved in the signature but this comparison itself works for any family of opens.

lean.statement: theorem alternatingCechComputes (X : Scheme.{u}) {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (U : I → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) (F : X.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w}) (S : SiteCechComplex U (fun i ↦ homOfLE (le_top : U i ≤ ⊤))) : ∃ A : CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{max v w} ℕ, ∃ e : ∀ p : ℕ, A.X p ≅ AddCommGrpCat.of (∀ t : {t : Fin (p + 1) → I // StrictMono t}, F.obj (op (S.W p t.1))), ∃ r : S.complex F ⟶ A, (∀ (p : ℕ) (s : A.X p) (t : {t : Fin (p + 2) → I // StrictMono t}), (e (p + 1)).hom ((A.d p (p + 1)) s) t = ∑ j : Fin (p + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val • F.map (S.indexMap t.1 j.succAbove).op ((e p).hom s ⟨t.1 ∘ j.succAbove, t.2.comp (Fin.strictMono_succAbove j)⟩)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ) (s : S.cochains F p) (t : {t : Fin (p + 1) → I // StrictMono t}), (e p).hom ((r.f p) s) t = s t.1) ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap r p)
lean.note: The chosen-intersection binder S uses def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex directly; its universal properties force each W to be the actual intersection in the poset of opens. Simultaneous degree identifications pin the signed differential and restriction components; IsIso is imposed on the homologyMap of that restriction. Scheme, index, and coefficient universes are independent.
